Two-storey wings and taller entrance/oriel tower survive at skyline; sash frames, parapets and conservatory restore at district; tracery and small masonry/metal details resolve at street/closeup. Synthetic neighbors are style fixtures.

fidelityReview.scope: Model the named Gothic residence with its entrance tower, brick/stone facade and conservatory. It is a separate building from Kensington Palace.
fidelityReview.notes: Full surviving residence and south conservatory accepted at the agreed approximate medium-fi scope. Cleared Qualla media checked first; only the modern attribution-only facade and unrelated Kensington Palace map were published, so neither is active imagery. Two exact public-domain original illustrations from architect C.J.Richardson’s The Englishman’s House were individually inspected: complete exterior perspective p476 and ground plan p479. The primary Gutenberg catalog explicitly marks the book public domain in the USA and identifies Richardson1806–1871; the selected image links, catalog/book snapshots and exact bytes are bound. The drawings establish the sash-window wings, projecting central oriel/entry, open parapets, chimney rhythm and side conservatory. Primary Survey of London1973text independently describes the surviving buff-brick/Bath-stone body and1924alterations: bell turret removed, steps/wooden porch changed, conservatory windows changed and its sloping roof replaced by flat roof. That flat-roof statement applies to the conservatory, not a surveyed description of the entire main roof. Historic England1266971 independently identifies the symmetrical Gothic facade, diagonal buttresses, sash openings, central oriel and entrance canopy. Existing geometry agrees at medium-fi scope; historical turret is correctly omitted. No original scope removed or geometry rebuilt. Precise tracery, doorway/porch profiles, secondary openings, main-roof slopes/drainage, conservatory glazing subdivisions and current fixtures remain estimates. Original native footprint, heading, independent ground and source/runtime/four LOD bytes retained. Fourteen current portable/shared views inspected and retained; nineteen fresh current-identity detail/LOD frames inspected. No reference pixels embedded.

geometryValidation.notes: Exact targeted regeneration, imported master integrity, four actual LOD digests, strict medium-fi budgets, source/scene/terrain schemas and repeated30tick state pass. All geometry, native map/ground and global placement bytes remain unchanged.

limitations: Full surviving exterior reviewed with two original public-domain C.J.Richardson illustrations and independent primary Survey of London/heritage architectural descriptions. The earlier attribution-only photograph is excluded; no measured survey or interior.
Buff masonry, white sash surrounds, entrance bay and open parapet rhythm are represented. Fine carvings, exact tracery and secondary elevation openings are simplified interpretations.

The former bell turret is omitted following the primary1924alteration history. The documented sloping-to-flat roof change applies to the south conservatory. Exact main-roof slopes/drainage, conservatory glazing and hidden rear details remain medium-fi interpretations.

Independent coarse terrain determines host contact. The ambassadorial flag, garden hedges, security fixtures, surrounding streets and interiors are omitted. Local reference photography is not embedded or redistributed.
